h1:
River Fish & Prawns in Ang Thong
8 Riverside Spots, Fresh From the Chao Phraya
intro: Ang Thong sits between the Chao Phraya and the Noi rivers, so the food locals are proudest of is river fish and freshwater prawns — netted by villagers and delivered to restaurants fresh every day. You'll find redtail catfish, blue sheatfish, clown knifefish, and big fat river prawns. Plenty of riverside places do tom yum, salt-grilled fish and grilled prawns so well that Bangkok folks drive out just to eat here. We picked 8 spots that are genuinely open, with locations and rough prices so you can plan ahead.

blocks.html: The whole appeal of eating river fish in Ang Thong is freshness. Most restaurants sit right on the water and take their catch from local fishermen. Firm redtail catfish goes into tom yum or gets blanched for dipping, blue sheatfish becomes choo chee, and clown knifefish is scraped into fish cakes. The big river prawns, dripping with roe, get grilled or salt-roasted and eaten with hot rice by the river. This is the kind of meal that makes people passing through pull over.

blocks.text: 8 River Fish & Prawn Spots Along the Water in Ang Thong

items.name: Ruen Pool Thong (on the Chao Phraya, near Wat Tan Chet Cho)
items.blurb: A wooden house right on the Chao Phraya, where the draw is river fish that villagers deliver fresh every day. Standouts include tom yum redtail catfish, choo chee blue sheatfish, fried sole, clown-knifefish fish cakes and grilled river prawns. If you're already visiting Wat Tan Chet Cho, just swing by — it's right next door.
items.meta: Talat Kruat, Mueang district · open daily 10:00–21:00 · tel 089-410-7387

items.name: Krua Khun Kung, Riverside Raft (Pa Mok)
items.blurb: A restaurant on a floating raft in the Pa Mok area, laid-back and known for fresh ingredients at fair prices. The dishes people order most are river prawns in rakam-sour soup, herb-fried sea bass, fish stir-fried with lemongrass, ho mok steamed in a coconut, and old-style sour curry. Great for families or bigger groups.
items.meta: Route 3501, Pa Mok subdistrict, Pa Mok district · open 11:00–22:00
items.price: ฿200–400 per head · river prawns sold by the kilo

items.name: Niramit Restaurant (Sali Rong, Wiset Chai Chan, on the Noi river)
items.blurb: A restaurant on the Noi river over on the Wiset Chai Chan side, known for tom yum with big chunks of redtail catfish, grilled river prawns, pad thai with fresh prawns, and a lineup of country-style Thai dishes. Lots of space, easy parking, and it's been open long enough to be a regular haunt for locals around there.
items.meta: Sali Rong, Wiset Chai Chan district · Mon–Fri 10:00–20:00 · Sat–Sun 9:00–20:00 · tel 081-852-4777

items.name: Bok Tor Restaurant (Ban Hae, right on the canal)
items.blurb: A restaurant on the canal in the Ban Hae area. The highlights are kaeng khua with pickled bamboo and redtail catfish, grilled river prawns, salt-fried river prawns, and prawns 'krabueang' style. Finish with ice cream served in a cold coconut. True to its name (bok tor means 'word of mouth'), this is a place locals genuinely pass along.
items.meta: Ban Hae, Mueang district · open daily 10:00–21:00 (kitchen closes 20:30) · tel 065-246-2288

items.name: Fa Sai Restaurant, on the Chao Phraya (Chaiyo)
items.blurb: A restaurant on the Chao Phraya in the Chaiyo area, with an open river view that's perfect for settling in through the evening. The menu runs to river fish and Thai-style seafood — grilled prawns, salt-grilled fish, tom yum — and it's easy to come as a group and share. Worth calling ahead on weekends, since it gets busy.
items.meta: Chaiyo district, on the Chao Phraya river

items.name: Ruen Rim Nam Seafood
items.blurb: A wooden riverside place with a seafood lean, offering river prawns, river fish and ocean seafood. The standouts are big grilled prawns and fresh fried or steamed fish. Shady and relaxed — a good spot for an unhurried lunch.
items.meta: Within Ang Thong province (check the pin on Amazing Thailand before you go)

items.name: Canalside spots around Ang Thong town (cluster of fish & prawn places)
items.blurb: Ang Thong town and its surroundings have several fish-and-prawn spots lined up along the canal, known for friendly prices and fresh river catch. Good for a lunch break while you're temple-hopping in town. Walk past, read the menus out front, and pick the one with the most people sitting — that's your shortcut to deciding.
items.meta: Mueang Ang Thong district · many open from midday into the evening

items.name: Riverside rafts around Pa Mok–Chaiyo (the raft-vibe option)
items.blurb: If you like eating on a floating raft, the Pa Mok and Chaiyo areas have a few raft restaurants to choose from. Cool breeze, boats drifting past — order grilled river prawns, salt-grilled fish and tom yum, settle in and soak up the full riverside feel. Great for a weekend when you want to eat slowly.
items.meta: Pa Mok / Chaiyo districts · most open from midday into the evening

blocks.title: How to order and get your money's worth
blocks.html: River fish and prawns are mostly priced by weight, so before you order, always ask the price per kilo and the size of the fish or prawn — that way there's no surprise when the bill comes. Big river prawns are full of roe, so grilling or salt-roasting brings out the richness best, while redtail catfish is best in tom yum or blanched for dipping.

blocks.text: River Fish & Prawns: What Should You Order?

blocks.html: First time here and not sure what to get? These are the dishes Ang Thong's riverside restaurants do well and order often. Pick a mix of both fish and prawn so you get the full picture of what this stretch of river produces.

items: Tom yum redtail catfish — firm, springy catfish in a rich, punchy tom yum; the signature dish at almost every place.
Choo chee blue sheatfish — fried blue fish in coconut choo chee curry, fragrant with curry paste and great over hot rice.
Grilled / salt-roasted river prawns — big prawns full of roe, grilled in the shell and peeled to eat with seafood dipping sauce.
Clown-knifefish fish cakes — scraped knifefish meat fried into bouncy cakes; a snack or a side, your call.
Salt-grilled fish — a whole river fish grilled in salt, the flesh peeled off and dipped in jaew sauce — fresh and sweet.
Kaeng khua / sour curry with river fish — bold country flavors that go perfectly with hot steamed rice.

blocks.text: Planning a riverside meal that works

items.name: Lunch while temple-hopping
items.blurb: Do the temples in Ang Thong town in the morning, then stop at a canalside spot in town, or at Ruen Pool Thong near Wat Tan Chet Cho, around midday.

items.name: Chilled riverside dinner
items.blurb: Pick a raft restaurant or a Chao Phraya spot around Pa Mok–Chaiyo, catch the cool evening breeze, and order grilled prawns and salt-grilled fish to share.

blocks.title: What to know before you go
blocks.html: Many riverside places get packed on weekends and Buddhist holy days, so if you're coming as a group, call ahead to book a table. Some spots prefer cash over bank transfer, so keep some on you. Fresh fish and prawns can be limited each day — come late morning to midday and you'll have more to choose from.

faq.q: Which river fish and prawn spots in Ang Thong on the Chao Phraya do you recommend?
faq.a: Ruen Pool Thong, on the Chao Phraya near Wat Tan Chet Cho, is known for river fish delivered fresh daily. Krua Khun Kung's riverside raft at Pa Mok stands out for river prawns and the raft atmosphere. And Niramit in Wiset Chai Chan is known for tom yum with big chunks of redtail catfish. All three sit right on the water and source their ingredients from the local rivers.

faq.q: Roughly how much do grilled river prawns cost in Ang Thong?
faq.a: River prawns are usually priced by weight and size. Overall, a river fish and prawn meal by the water runs around 200–400 THB per head, and ordering big prawns by the kilo pushes it higher. Always ask the price per kilo and the size before you order.

faq.q: What dishes are popular with Ang Thong river fish?
faq.a: The popular ones are tom yum redtail catfish, choo chee blue sheatfish, clown-knifefish fish cakes, salt-grilled fish, and sour or kaeng khua curry with river fish. Redtail catfish suits tom yum because the flesh is firm, while blue sheatfish goes well with coconut choo chee.

faq.q: Do you need to book a table ahead at riverside restaurants in Ang Thong?
faq.a: On weekdays you can mostly just walk in, but weekends, Buddhist holy days and festival periods get busy. If you're coming as a big group or want a riverside table, call ahead to book — and allow extra time, since some fresh items sell out fast.

faq.q: Is Ang Thong far from Bangkok? Can you do a day trip and eat by the river?
faq.a: Ang Thong is about 100 km from Bangkok — roughly 1.5–2 hours by car — so a day trip is easy. Plenty of people drive out for a riverside lunch and then go temple-hopping in the same day.
